name: The six destroyers of yoga (HYP 1.15)
description: Overeating, overexertion, too much talk, clinging to rules, the company of people and unsteadiness destroy yoga.
antidotes: enthusiasm, boldness, patience, knowledge of truth, determination, renouncing company (HYP 1.16)

name: Overeating (atyāhāra)
description: Eating too much; first of the six destroyers (HYP 1.15); listed among things to avoid (SS 3.33; DYŚ 65).

name: Clinging to rules (niyamagraha)
description: Rigid adherence to (unsuitable) observances such as early-morning bathing or fasting (HYP 1.15; Gorakṣa's saying 1.61).

name: The company of people (janasaṅga)
description: Mixing with people; its abandonment is among the six promoters (HYP 1.15–16).

name: Improper breath-control
description: Breath forced or held unskilfully 'kills the practitioner' and causes hiccup, asthma, cough and pain in head, ears and eyes (HYP 2.15–17); breath must be drawn and released slowly, never held too long (GŚ 51).
antidotes: gradual, skilful practice under a guru (HYP 2.15, 2.18)

name: Impurities in the channels
description: Channels clogged with impurities prevent the breath from entering the central channel, so unmanī cannot arise (HYP 2.4; GS 5.35).

name: Excess of fat and phlegm
description: An excess of fat (medas) or phlegm (śleṣman) calls for the six acts before breath-control; those whose humours are balanced need not do them (HYP 2.21, 2.36).

name: The fall of bindu
description: Loss of bindu is death, its retention life (HYP 3.88); in the ghaṭa stage women drawn by the yogin's beauty are a great obstacle, since union destroys bindu and shortens life (DYŚ 77–79).

name: The obstacles at the start of practice (Dattātreyayogaśāstra)
description: Laziness, boasting, the company of rogues, mantra-sādhana, alchemy (dhātuvāda) and talk of food — mirages to be recognized and abandoned (DYŚ 47–48).

name: Laziness (ālasya)
description: The first obstacle at the beginning of practice (DYŚ 47).

name: Hypocrisy of the unrealised (dambha)
description: Wearing an ascetic's garb or talking of yoga without practice (HYP 1.65–66; DYŚ 39–46, 'for the sake of penis and belly'); speaking of knowledge before the breath enters the middle path is 'deceitful prattle' (HYP 4.114).

name: The three kinds of obstacle (Śiva Saṃhitā)
description: Obstacles to liberation in the form of enjoyment (learning, arts, wealth, family, sense-objects), of dharma (meditation-objects, mantra, gifts, fame, public works, sacrifices, vows, pilgrimages) and of knowledge (SS 5.2–8); many terrible obstacles, to be overcome by perseverance and the praṇava (3.47–48).
antidotes: repetition of the long praṇava in solitude (SS 3.48)

name: Powers as obstacles
description: The powers of the ghaṭa stage are obstacles to the great accomplishment; displaying them draws disciples and distracts from practice (DYŚ 91–94).
antidotes: concealment; living as if dull or deaf (DYŚ 93)

name: Faults from practising yoga at the wrong time or place
description: Beginning yoga in a distant land (no trust), forest (no food), capital or crowd (exposure), or in winter, summer or the rains brings failure or disease (GS 5.3–9).
antidotes: a hidden hut in a good land; beginning in spring or autumn (GS 5.5–9)
